prompt:
Continue this exact laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage for 6 seconds. Same camera, viewpoint, lighting, colours, image quality and anatomy as the input image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frame):
A circular laparoscopic view shows the dissection of the hepatocystic triangle. A metallic fenestrated grasper enters from the lower-left edge, holding the pale pink and yellowish gallbladder neck to provide lateral traction. A second instrument with a grey insulated shaft and open metallic jaws enters from the lower-right edge, positioned against the darkly cauterized tissue bed. The dissected area reveals a small window with a bluish tubular structure and dark red charred tissue. Reddish-brown liver parenchyma is visible on the upper right and upper left, while yellowish-orange adipose tissue rests at the bottom of the frame. There are no surgical clips, no active bleeding, and no smoke present in the scene.

One surgical step happens (chosen by a patient world model): A laparoscopic electrocautery hook: a slim grey insulated shaft ending in a small bent metal tip comes into view along its shaft (or, if it is already in view, moves to the cystic plate). It makes short, deliberate strokes, stripping fat and connective tissue away from the cystic plate.

Instruments already in view: the grasper and the scissors. An instrument never changes into another instrument. Before the hook arrives, any instrument in its way slides straight back out of view along its own shaft; the others stay where they are.

By the end of the clip: the cystic plate is partly freed: some fat and connective tissue has been stripped from it.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands; bleeding; clips; cutting.
explanation: Dissecting the cystic plate with the hook advances exposure to 0.56 and satisfies two of three CVS criteria without causing bleeding or rule violations, consistent with VID15_00497 and VID15_00521. Following hook dissection in this phase, the surgeon most frequently adjusts traction on the gallbladder with the grasper (VID15_00497, VID15_00521, VID15_00631) or proceeds to clipping (VID43_01073).
